ideas.name: LexiLens
ideas.niche: Neurodivergent-focused typography testing and accessibility comparison
ideas.problem: Users with dyslexia face high friction when trying to identify which specific font families actually reduce visual crowding or letter swapping for their unique visual processing needs.
ideas.targetUser: Neurodivergent students, UX/UI designers building accessible products, and educators or occupational therapists assisting students with literacy tools.
coreFeatures: Real-time live text rendering sandbox
Curated library of high-legibility fonts (e.g., OpenDyslexic, Lexend)
Split-screen A/B comparison mode
Visual stress reduction controls (tinted backgrounds and line-height adjustment)
Simulated reading speed meter
realDependencies: Google Fonts API
Web Speech API (for text-to-speech)
Firebase for saving custom font configurations
Google Analytics for UX research
ideas.emulationStrategy: The prototype will use a local JSON manifest to store font metadata and local font files to simulate the Google Fonts API. An asynchronous 'fetchFont' function will be used with a randomized setTimeout (500ms–1500ms) to trigger realistic loading spinners. The Reading Speed meter will be emulated using a mathematical formula that calculates a 'fake' WPM based on the input string length and a randomized coefficient. Accessibility overlays will be handled via real-time CSS variable injection to simulate a high-fidelity interactive experience.

The impact of typography on cognitive load is a critical area of study for neurodivergent learners. When characters are too close together, a phenomenon known as visual crowding occurs, making it difficult for the eye to distinguish between individual letters. By adjusting line height, letter spacing, and selecting specific typeface weights, we can create a "visual runway" that guides the reader through the text more effectively. Try changing the background tint to a soft cream or pale blue to reduce visual stress and glare.

ideas.name: VeloText
ideas.problem: High-motion video backgrounds (camera shakes, rapid zooms, fast pans) often render text captions unreadable, causing viewer drop-off on TikTok, Reels, and Shorts.
ideas.targetUser: Gen Z and Millennial short-form video creators, professional social media editors, and digital marketing managers producing high-energy vertical content.
coreFeatures: Motion Simulator: Sliders to mimic camera shake frequency, zoom jitter, and panning speed.
Typography Sandbox: Real-time styling for font weight, stroke thickness, drop shadows, and text-box opacity.
Legibility Scorer: An algorithmic score that predicts text readability based on motion intensity and contrast.
UI Safe-Zone Overlay: Visual guides for platform-specific UI (like TikTok buttons and descriptions) to prevent text overlap.
realDependencies: FFmpeg.wasm for client-side video manipulation and motion rendering
Google Fonts API for dynamic typography loading
AWS S3 or Cloudinary for high-resolution video asset storage
Canvas API for real-time text-over-video compositing
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will simulate motion by applying CSS 'shake' keyframe animations and 'scale' transforms to a standard HTML5 video element based on slider inputs. The Legibility Scorer will be a mathematical heuristic calculating (font_size * contrast_ratio) / motion_intensity. To simulate video uploads, the app will use a 2-second `setTimeout` with a mock progress bar, then utilize `URL.createObjectURL` to load the user's local file into the player as if it were fetched from a cloud server.

ideas.name: SipSafe
ideas.niche: Real-time global tap water safety and consumption guidance for international travelers.
ideas.problem: The health anxiety and uncertainty travelers face when trying to determine if tap water is safe to drink in foreign countries, caused by fragmented, outdated, and contradictory information found in forums and blogs.
ideas.targetUser: International backpackers, digital nomads, and families traveling to developing or high-risk regions who require immediate, actionable hydration instructions to avoid waterborne illness.
coreFeatures: Instant Visual Safety Rating (Green/Yellow/Red color-coded dashboard)
Actionable Consumption Protocols (e.g., 'Boil required', 'Ice is safe', 'Avoid brushing teeth')
Nearby Potable Water Refill Station Locator
Crowdsourced 'Live Alert' feed for sudden contamination reports
realDependencies: Google Maps Platform for geolocation and refill station discovery
WHO (World Health Organization) environmental health datasets
Firebase Realtime Database for user-reported safety updates
Weather API to correlate seasonal flooding/monsoon patterns with water safety risk
ideas.emulationStrategy: The app will use a local JSON lookup table containing a curated dataset of 100 global cities with pre-set safety tiers and protocols. A 'Mock API' wrapper will use async/await with a 'latency simulator' to introduce randomized delays between 600ms and 1800ms for every search. To mimic real-time crowdsourcing, a 'Noise Generator' function will periodically inject randomized 'Community Alerts' (e.g., 'High sediment reported in Marrakech') into the UI state. The map feature will be emulated by displaying a high-resolution static map image with custom SVG overlays representing water stations.

ideas.name: RouteFlow
ideas.problem: Inaccurate cable length estimation leading to costly project delays due to under-ordering or significant budget waste from excessive over-ordering.
ideas.targetUser: Field AV technicians, IT network engineers, and data center infrastructure managers who require precision in bulk procurement and installation planning.
coreFeatures: Dynamic Path Modeler: Input horizontal, vertical, and diagonal distances with bend radius constraints.
Complexity & Slack Algorithm: Automated slack calculation based on cable type (Fiber, CAT6, HDMI) and containment method (tray, conduit, or plenum).
BOM (Bill of Materials) Export: Instant generation of professional procurement lists in PDF and CSV formats.
Project Scoping Workspace: Organize multiple cable runs into single job profiles for batch ordering and budget tracking.
realDependencies: Firebase Authentication for user accounts and project syncing
PostgreSQL/Supabase for relational data storage of complex routing paths
Cloud-based PDF Generation API for BOM exports
AWS S3 for storing site-specific floor plans and cable diagrams
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will use a local JSON-based mock database to simulate CRUD operations. All 'API calls' will be wrapped in a service layer that uses setTimeout to inject variable latency (800ms to 2500ms) to simulate real-world network conditions. Authentication will be faked via a simple state toggle that mimics a 'Logged In' status without actual credential verification. PDF exports will be emulated by downloading a static, pre-made sample file instead of generating one dynamically.

ideas.name: GlyphDash
ideas.niche: Rapid-response, low-complexity instructional signage for micro-events.
ideas.problem: Non-designers waste excessive time in complex software trying to create legible, standardized, and printable directional icons for immediate event setup.
ideas.targetUser: Pop-up market vendors, community festival coordinators, and small cafe owners who need to create safety and wayfinding signs on-site or on short notice.
coreFeatures: Instant-Select Icon Library (ISO-standard compliant)
High-Contrast Color Presets (Safety Yellow, Emergency Red, Wayfinding Blue)
Dynamic Text Overlay with optimized sans-serif fonts
One-Click PDF Export for standard paper sizes (A4, US Letter)
realDependencies: SVG Asset Management System
Server-side PDF rendering engine (e.g., Puppeteer or ReportLab)
Cloud Storage for saved templates (e.g., AWS S3)
User Authentication (e.g., Firebase Auth)
ideas.emulationStrategy: Replace the PDF engine with a client-side SVG-to-Blob generator that mimics file creation. Use a local mock-API service that returns JSON icon metadata with a hardcoded 1.5s-2.5s delay to simulate network latency. Simulate 'Saving to Cloud' by updating a local state variable and showing a loading spinner, followed by a 'Success' toast notification, rather than performing actual network requests.
